dedupe_keys.name: gengeo coupled reservoir electricity and cost geothermal simulator

description: genGEO is an open-source, object-oriented Python simulator that couples a geothermal reservoir model with power plant electricity generation and cost calculations. It was written by Benjamin M. Adams and Philipp Schädle and is hosted by the GEG group at ETH Zurich, and it is designed to be extended to any geothermal or power generation scenario. The shipped example models a CO2 plume geothermal (CPG) system and solves it over a range of reservoir depths and permeabilities, and an optimisation mode is included in the tests. The method is location-independent. It needs Python 3.7 with pandas, SciPy, CoolProp and xlrd, with a conda environment file provided, and version 0.0.1 of December 2020 is archived on Zenodo. The repository licence is LGPL-2.1 at no cost, while the Zenodo archive lists CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: only one early release exists, the last commit dates from July 2021, and the example runs for a long time. Simulation uses are techno-economic optimisation of geothermal power plants and screening of sites for capacity planning. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
